title: 오늘은 제가 점심을 살 테니 새로 생긴 한식당에 가요
en: I'll buy lunch today, so let's go to the Korean restaurant that just opened

items.ex: 저 건물 1층에는 스파게티가 맛있는 레스토랑이 있어요.
items.exen: On the ground floor of that building there's a restaurant with great spaghetti.
This bank's main branch is in Seoul.

items.mean: snack shop — tteokbokki, gimbap, ramyeon and the like
items.ex: 가영 씨는 떡볶이와 김밥을 좋아해서 분식집에 자주 가요.
items.exen: Gayeong likes tteokbokki and gimbap and often goes to a snack shop.

items.mean: branch (a second shop opened by the main one)
items.ex: 대전에서 제일 유명한 빵집의 분점이 서울에도 생겼다.
items.exen: A branch of Daejeon's most famous bakery has opened in Seoul too.

items.ex: 뷔페에는 여러 종류의 음식이 다양하게 있어요.
items.exen: A buffet has all sorts of different food.

items.ex: 친구와 함께 일식집에 가서 초밥을 먹었어요.
items.exen: I went to a Japanese restaurant with a friend and had sushi.

items.ex: 자장면을 먹으러 집 근처에 있는 중국집에 갔다.
items.exen: I went to the Chinese restaurant near my house to have jjajangmyeon.

items.ex: 명동에 있는 갈비 가게는 외국인에게도 인기가 많아서 외국에도 체인점을 냈다.
items.exen: The galbi place in Myeongdong is popular with foreigners too, so it has opened chain branches abroad.

items.ex: 요즘은 외국에도 한국 음식을 파는 한식당이 많이 생겼어요.
items.exen: These days a lot of Korean restaurants selling Korean food have opened abroad as well.

items.mean: to be satisfying, to be pleasing
items.ex: 작가는 만족스러운 사진이 나올 때까지 사진을 찍었다.
items.exen: The photographer kept shooting until a satisfying picture came out.

items.mean: to feel like too much, to be a burden on you (money, obligation, attention)
items.exen: My friend gave me an expensive present, and it feels like too much.

items.ex: 그 식당은 음식 맛은 좋았지만 서비스가 불만족스러웠어요.
items.exen: The food at that restaurant tasted good, but the service was unsatisfactory.

items.mean: to be unfriendly, to be rude (service)
items.ex: 저 식당은 점원이 불친절해서 자주 가지 않아요.
items.exen: The staff at that restaurant are unfriendly, so I don't go often.

items.mean: to be crowded, to be packed
items.exen: It was going-home time, so the roads were packed with cars.

items.mean: to be cheap, to be inexpensive (price)
items.ex: 이 식당은 음식 가격이 저렴해서 학생들에게 인기가 많아요.
items.exen: This restaurant's prices are low, so it's popular with students.

items.mean: to be messy, to be dirty, untidy
items.ex: 며칠 동안 청소를 못 해서 방이 지저분해요.
items.exen: I haven't been able to clean for a few days, so my room is messy.

items.mean: to be kind, to be friendly
items.ex: 한국 생활이 처음에는 힘들었지만 친절한 이웃들 덕분에 빨리 적응했어요.
items.exen: Life in Korea was hard at first, but thanks to kind neighbours I settled in quickly.

items.mean: to be pleasant and comfortable (clean, airy, roomy)
items.ex: 식당이 깔끔하고 넓어서 쾌적한 분위기에서 식사할 수 있었습니다.
items.exen: The restaurant was neat and spacious, so we could eat in a pleasant atmosphere.

items.mean: to be quiet, to be uncrowded (↔ 붐비다)
items.exen: During the holidays there are no students, so the campus is quiet.

grammar.def_ko: 1. 앞 절을 뒤 절의 내용에 대한 조건이 되게 하겠다는 의지를 나타내는 표현. 2. 앞 절이 뒤 절의 내용에 대한 조건이라고 강하게 추측하여 나타내는 표현.
grammar.def_en: 1. The speaker's intention, offered as the condition for what follows — 'I'll do A, so (you) do B'. 2. A confident guess about A, given as the reason for the suggestion or request in B — 'it'll probably be A, so let's B'. Either way the second clause is normally a suggestion, request or command, not a plain statement.

ex.ko: 내가 지금 잠깐 나가야 하는데 아까 주문한 피자 배달 오면 대신 좀 받아 줘.
ex.en: I have to pop out for a bit — could you take the pizza I ordered when it arrives?

ex.ko: 그래. 내가 대신 받아 줄 테니 걱정하지 마.
ex.en: Sure. I'll take it for you, so don't worry. (intention)

ex.ko: 지난번에 빌려 간 책 오늘 줄 수 있어?
ex.en: Can you give me back the book you borrowed last time today?

ex.ko: 얼른 읽을 테니 조금만 기다려 줘.
ex.en: I'll read it quickly, so give me just a little longer.

ex.ko: 오후에 비가 올 테니 우산을 가져가세요.
ex.en: It'll probably rain this afternoon, so take an umbrella. (guess)
Shall we go to the cinema on Saturday?

ex.ko: 주말에는 사람이 많을 테니 가지 말자.
ex.en: It'll be crowded at the weekend, so let's not go.

grammar.info_ko: 뜻 1은 동사와 결합하고, 뜻 2는 동사, 형용사, '명사+이다'와 결합한다. 받침이 있으면 '-을 테니', 받침이 없거나 'ㄹ' 받침이면 '-ㄹ 테니'를 쓴다.
grammar.info_en: After a final consonant -을 테니, otherwise -ㄹ 테니 (a ㄹ stem just drops the ㄹ: 살다 → 살 테니). Meaning 1 (intention) takes verbs only — the first table; meaning 2 (guess) also takes adjectives and (명사)이다 — the second table. -(으)ㄹ 테니까 is the same thing and just as common. Compare -(으)ㄹ 텐데 from 8과, which sets up a worry or a contrast instead of a reason.

table2.caption: 뜻 2 · Strong guess — 동사, 형용사, '(명사)이다'와 모두 결합해요

기본형

grammar.tag: so that… / to the point that…
grammar.def_ko: 1. 뒤에 나오는 행위의 목적을 나타낼 때 쓰는 연결 어미. 2. 뒤에 나오는 동작, 작용의 정도나 한계를 나타낼 때 쓰는 연결 어미.
grammar.def_en: 1. Marks the goal of the action that follows — 'so that ~', 'in order that ~'. 2. Marks how far that action goes — '(so much) that ~', 'until ~'.

ex.ko: 나타샤 씨, 한국어 말하기 대회에서 발표할 때 정말 한국 사람 같았어요.
ex.en: Natasha, when you presented at the Korean speech contest you sounded just like a Korean.

ex.ko: 정말요? 고마워요. 대회에서 실수하지 않도록 연습을 많이 했거든요.
ex.en: Really? Thank you. I practised a lot so that I wouldn't make mistakes at the contest. (purpose)

ex.ko: 이 영화를 보고 배꼽이 빠지도록 웃었어요.
ex.en: I laughed my head off watching this film. (extent — lit. 'till my belly button fell out')
Is it that funny? I'll have to watch it too.

ex.ko: 친구 생일을 잊지 않도록 달력에 표시했어요.
ex.en: I marked it on the calendar so I wouldn't forget my friend's birthday.

ex.ko: 새벽 두 시가 넘도록 숙제를 하느라 잠을 못 잤다.
ex.en: I was doing homework until past two in the morning, so I didn't get any sleep. (extent)

grammar.info_ko: 동사와 결합한다. 받침에 관계없이 '-도록'을 쓴다. 부정은 '-지 않도록', '-지 못하도록'을 쓴다.
grammar.info_en: Attaches to verbs, and the form never changes — always -도록, with or without a final consonant. Negative: -지 않도록 / -지 못하도록 ('so that you don't ~'). Meaning 2 usually comes with a time or degree phrase: 밤이 새도록, 목이 아프도록, 배꼽이 빠지도록. Close to -게 for purpose (실수하지 않게 = 실수하지 않도록), but -도록 sounds a touch more formal.
